newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine peso ends higher in volatile trade.
newsitem.headline: Philippine peso ends higher in volatile trade.

text.p: * Value drops to $151 million from $283.7 million
The Philippine peso ended higher at 26.254 to the dollar on Tuesday from the previous 26.265 as banks sold the U.S. currency following a rise in Central Bank overnight rates, traders said.
"The Central Bank used its overnight borrowing rate as a tool to curb speculation in the foreign exchange market," said one dealer.
The peso peaked at 26.224. Traders said the Central Bank sold $27 million at 26.26 out of the $151 million that changed hands.
The Central Bank surprised banks at the start of the trading when it raised its borrowing rate, dealers said.
"The move disheartened banks which sold down the peso on Monday following the steep fall of the overnight and treasury bill rates," said another trader.
The market will closely watch fresh developments on the military tension between Iraq and the United States on Wednesday. --DOLLY AGLAY (632) 841-8936, FAX 817-6267
